chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Hasan bin Mahbub, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: What is the limit of openhandedness?
He said: You extract from your property the right which Allah has obliged upon you, and you put it in its place.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic definition of true generosity or openhandedness according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq defining 'sakhā' (generosity) not as supererogatory giving, but as the precise fulfillment of obligatory dues (ḥuqūq Allāh) from one's wealth. This definition elevates legal compliance to the status of ethical virtue, emphasizing that true generosity begins with the correct allocation of what is already due to God and the community. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the integration of fiqh (jurisprudence) and akhlāq (ethics), where fulfilling rights is the foundation of spiritual generosity.
